---
title: "Basic Commands"
---

Everything you will ever do in R comes down to two basic tasks: creating a new R object or processing an existing R
object. That might sound abstract right now, but we'll build up the core ideas through the following steps.

1. [Fundamental Interactions](/tutorials/basic_commands/fundamentals.qmd): Using R as a calculator
1. [Objects](/tutorials/basic_commands/objects.qmd): Storing data values for subsequent calculations
1. [Extended Operators](/tutorials/basic_commands/extended_operators.qmd): Powers, roots, and other useful functions
1. [Logical Comparisons](/tutorials/basic_commands/logical_comparisons.qmd): Asking R `TRUE`/`FALSE` questions
1. [Comments](/tutorials/basic_commands/comments.qmd): Leaving notes in your code
1. [Environments](/tutorials/basic_commands/environments.qmd) *(optional)*: Where R keeps your objects

By the end of this module, you'll be able to run calculations in R, interpret the output, and write your own simple
expressions. These basic interactions are the foundation every R-based data analysis builds on.
